title: WAL commit-path: widen group-commit window and batch writer flushes
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 opens a fixed per-commit stall that rarely collects siblings at 5 terminals, while wal_writer_flush_after=0 forces per-write flushing; WAL sync latency (0.13ms) and wal_wait persist.
mechanism: The WAL commit path is the only storage-side anomaly: wal_waiting_backends max=1 with sync_average_ms=0.13 and write_average_ms=0.022, host_io stalls zero, so the cost is sync frequency/queueing, not disk saturation. commit_delay=100us is too short to collect the 5 terminals' commits yet still adds a fixed stall to every commit; commit_siblings=2 gates group commit too eagerly. Widening the collection window to 500us and raising the activation threshold to 3 lets concurrent commits coalesce into one fsync, while wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) batches background writer flushes instead of flushing per write. Together these reduce syncs per transaction and drain the WAL wait queue, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88); reducing commit-path queueing shortens InsertTweet and mixed-transaction stalls, freeing terminal slots for the dominant read path.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps as WAL wait queue drains; bounded by client terminal saturation.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 and GetUserTweets p99 decrease slightly; overall p95 roughly unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window coalesces concurrent commits into fewer fsyncs, lowering average sync latency.
Batched writer flushes plus group commit drain the WAL wait queue.
Fewer commit-path stalls free terminal capacity for the dominant GetUserTweets path.

alternatives.statement: If the 500us window adds more stall than it saves, sync latency and TPS will not improve; a shorter window (200us) would then be preferred.
If WAL wait is incidental and terminal saturation is purely read-side, TPS stays flat despite lower sync latency.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves commit_delay=100us (too short to collect siblings, still a fixed stall) and wal_writer_flush_after=0 (per-write flushing). Widening the window to 500us with commit_siblings=3 and batching writer flushes to 256 reduces fsyncs per commit and drains the observed wal_wait queue.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units) within safe [0,1024]; 2MB flush batch reduces writer sync frequency versus per-write flushing.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: commit_delay 500, commit_siblings 3, wal_writer_flush_after 256
Wider group-commit window plus larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs

cross_domain_requirements: wal_compression already on; no further WAL volume reduction available
